scope: Targeted read-only BE98 checkpoint audit; historical outcomes are not a claim about current BE19000AI userspace.
current_policy: time64 first for all new and rebuilt components; source repair first, only proven individual legacy ABI boundaries may use a narrow fallback

findings.classification: actual observed hardware failure and source repair
findings.cause: get_mono passed libc struct timespec (16 bytes, tv_nsec offset8, time_t8) to legacy SYS_clock_gettime which wrote only8 bytes; canary bytes in the second half remained unchanged.
findings.symptom: ping reported roughly4294827ms after its initial packet while packets still passed.
findings.fix: When __USE_TIME_BITS64 is active, use libc clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, ts); keep time64. On the old BE98 kernel glibc handled ENOSYS from clock_gettime64 and translated legacy syscall results.
findings.recorded_validation: BE98 loopback, gateway, external ping and3-second deadline checks passed; applet list unchanged. Original record says no reboot or full firmware flash test.
findings.required_port_check: Match current BusyBox source/context before applying; a kernel time64 backport does not fix calls that still invoke the legacy syscall number with the wrong structure.

findings.classification: actual recorded relocation incompatibility; independent of time64
findings.component: Old armel libcrypt used by actual ASUSrc
findings.cause: Undefined __snprintf@GLIBC_PRIVATE no longer provided by new glibc.
findings.fix: Rebuild libxcrypt4.4.38 with obsolete ABI enabled, preserve existing versioned exports, test DES/MD5 crypt vectors and actualrc relocations.
findings.important_limit: The public symbol audit explicitly skipped GLIBC_PRIVATE; full loader relocation was necessary to catch this. It is not evidence that every retained binary was exercised and not justification to disable time64.

findings.classification: actual compiler default observation plus historical conservative ABI choice; not a reproduced time64 failure for every library
findings.observation: Preprocessing in the current audit directly confirms _TIME_BITS=64 and _FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 defaults. Earlier four-library migration and multiarch glibc build explicitly cleared them. The historical library probe asserted time_t4/off_t4.
findings.new_policy: Do not copy those broad -U flags into the new Ubuntu component defaults. Rebuild toward time64, inspect public structures/callers and retain an exception only where a specific incompatibility is proven. Keep glibc internal dual-ABI build rules distinct from application defaults.

positive_test_matrix: armel+armhf explicit_TIME_BITS64 and_FILE_OFFSET_BITS64 with size/offset assertions
post2038 timerfd and utimensat/statx plus large sparse-file offsets
monotonic progression/ping RTT/deadline under BusyBox repair
legacy_boundary_matrix: prove caller/callee widths and field offsets
check symbol versions and raw syscall structures separately
attempt checked source translation or process isolation before declaring exception
record component/version/reproducer/narrow fallback and retain positive time64 tests elsewhere
fresh_acceptance: No new firmware, package install, device write, network probe or BE19000AI userspace test was performed by this history audit.
